zh.q: 颜色不变，反应就停了吗？
zh.concl: 平衡是动态的：v(正) = v(逆) ≠ 0，各组分浓度不变。「颜色不变」不等于反应停了；判「往哪边移」要看 Q 与 K。
points: 两支试管的颜色不再变化，是达到平衡，不是反应停止。
示意放大里粒子一直双向转化：v(正) = v(逆) ≠ 0。
判断「是否平衡、往哪边移」，看浓度商 Q 与平衡常数 K 的大小。

zh.q: 再滴 5 滴 FeCl₃，红为什么更深？
zh.concl: 加反应物的瞬间 Q 变小（< K），正反应速率大于逆反应，平衡正向移动；达到新平衡时 Q 又回到 K。
points: 加 Fe³⁺ 的瞬间，Q = 26 < K = 146。
正向移动后 c(FeSCN²⁺) 从 0.379 升到 1.095 mmol/L。
新平衡时 Q 又等于 K：K 只随温度变。

zh.q: 加铁粉后红色为什么变浅？
zh.concl: 铁粉把 Fe³⁺ 还原成 Fe²⁺（2Fe³⁺ + Fe = 3Fe²⁺），c(Fe³⁺) 变小 → Q 变大，超过 K → 平衡逆向移动。
points: 铁粉把 Fe³⁺ 还原，c(Fe³⁺) 变小。
红色几乎褪掉（0.072 mmol/L），说明 FeSCN²⁺ 分解了。

zh.q: 滴 5 滴 NaOH，橙色为什么变黄？
zh.concl: 加碱中和了 H⁺，Q 变小（< K）→ 平衡正向移动：Cr₂O₇²⁻ + H₂O ⇌ 2CrO₄²⁻ + 2H⁺ 向生成 CrO₄²⁻（黄色）的方向移动。
points: 铬管里是 Cr₂O₇²⁻，橙色。
加碱中和 H⁺，Q 变小 → 正向，颜色转黄（CrO₄²⁻）。
对照管（不加碱）仍然是橙色。

zh.q: 接着滴 H₂SO₄，为什么又变回橙色？
zh.concl: 加酸使 c(H⁺) 变大，Q 变大（> K）→ 平衡逆向移动，溶液回到 Cr₂O₇²⁻ 的橙色。
points: 加酸使 c(H⁺) 变大，Q 变大 → 逆向，回到橙色。
与上一步合起来：同一支管，加碱变黄、加酸变橙。
两个方向都只是 Q 与 K 的比较，不需要另记一套规律。

zh.q: 同一只球，热水里红棕更深、冰水里变浅，为什么？
zh.concl: 2NO₂ ⇌ N₂O₄ 正反应放热（ΔH = −56.9 kJ/mol）：温度改的是 K 本身。升温 K 变小 → Q > K → 逆向（NO₂ 变多、红棕加深）；降温 K 变大 → Q < K → 正向（变浅）。
points: 温度改变的是 K 本身，浓度瞬间不变，Q 仍是 165.6。
0 ℃ 时 K = 1.4×10³ > Q → 正向，降到 4.824 mmol/L。

zh.q: 颜色背后，粒子在做什么？
zh.concl: 平衡不是「粒子不动」，而是两边转化速率相等；条件一改，两边速率不再相等，粒子数此消彼长，直到新的 Q = K。
points: 两边粒子一直在互相转化，从不停止。
平衡时两边速率相等，粒子数不再变化。
条件改变后一边明显变多，直到建立新的平衡。

zh.q: 为什么一定要等温度回到室温再比颜色？
zh.concl: 温度没恢复时，颜色里混着温度的影响，读数偏高；研究浓度的影响必须控制温度一致（教材「问题与讨论」第 1 条：控制变量、对比）。
points: 温度没恢复，颜色里混着温度效应。
教材要求：研究浓度影响时温度必须一致。

zh.q: 考核：能不能把红色调到 c ≥ 1.00 mmol/L 并稳住？
zh.concl: 选对试剂、按教材的量加（FeCl₃ 5 滴 → 1.095 mmol/L），并且用 c 而不是「颜色深不深」来判断。
points: 要选对滴瓶：FeCl₃ 5 滴 → 1.095；KSCN 5 滴只有 0.720。
达标看的是 c，不是「颜色深不深」。
多滴几滴也能达标（10 滴 → 1.440）。

en.q: If the color stops changing, has the reaction stopped?
en.concl: Equilibrium is dynamic: v(forward) = v(reverse) ≠ 0, and every concentration stays constant. "The color doesn't change" doesn't mean the reaction stopped; to tell which way it shifts, compare Q with K.
points: When the color in both tubes stops changing, equilibrium has been reached; the reaction hasn't stopped.
In the magnified view the particles keep converting both ways: v(forward) = v(reverse) ≠ 0.
To judge "is it at equilibrium, and which way does it shift", compare the reaction quotient Q with the equilibrium constant K.

en.q: Add 5 more drops of FeCl₃. Why does the red deepen?
en.concl: The instant reactant is added, Q drops (< K), the forward rate exceeds the reverse, and the equilibrium shifts forward; at the new equilibrium Q returns to K.
points: The instant Fe³⁺ is added, Q = 26 < K = 146.
After shifting forward, c(FeSCN²⁺) rises from 0.379 to 1.095 mmol/L.
At the new equilibrium Q equals K again: K only changes with temperature.

en.q: Why does the red fade after adding iron powder?
en.concl: Iron powder reduces Fe³⁺ to Fe²⁺ (2Fe³⁺ + Fe = 3Fe²⁺), so c(Fe³⁺) falls → Q rises above K → the equilibrium shifts in reverse.
points: Iron powder reduces Fe³⁺, lowering c(Fe³⁺).
Q = 1.5×10³ > K = 146: Q went up → reverse.
The red almost disappears (0.072 mmol/L), showing FeSCN²⁺ has broken down.

en.q: Add 5 drops of NaOH. Why does the orange turn yellow?
en.concl: Base neutralizes H⁺, Q falls (< K) → the equilibrium shifts forward: Cr₂O₇²⁻ + H₂O ⇌ 2CrO₄²⁻ + 2H⁺ moves toward CrO₄²⁻ (yellow).
points: The chromium tube holds Cr₂O₇²⁻, which is orange.
Base neutralizes H⁺, Q falls → forward, and the color turns yellow (CrO₄²⁻).
The control tube (no base) stays orange.

en.q: Now add H₂SO₄. Why does it turn back to orange?
en.concl: Acid raises c(H⁺), Q rises (> K) → the equilibrium shifts in reverse and the solution returns to the orange of Cr₂O₇²⁻.
points: Acid raises c(H⁺), Q rises → reverse, back to orange.
Together with the previous step: the same tube turns yellow with base and orange with acid.
Both directions are just Q compared with K; no separate rule to memorize.

en.q: The same bulb is darker red-brown in hot water and lighter in ice water. Why?
en.concl: In 2NO₂ ⇌ N₂O₄ the forward reaction is exothermic (ΔH = −56.9 kJ/mol): temperature changes K itself. Heating lowers K → Q > K → reverse (more NO₂, darker red-brown); cooling raises K → Q < K → forward (lighter).
points: Temperature changes K itself; the concentrations don't change instantly, so Q is still 165.6.
At 70 °C, K = 8.2 < Q → reverse, c(NO₂) 12.878 → 40.726 mmol/L.
At 0 °C, K = 1.4×10³ > Q → forward, falling to 4.824 mmol/L.

en.q: Behind the color, what are the particles doing?
en.concl: Equilibrium isn't "particles standing still" but equal conversion rates both ways; change a condition and the rates are no longer equal, one side grows as the other shrinks, until Q = K again.
points: Particles on both sides keep converting into each other and never stop.
At equilibrium both rates are equal and the particle counts stop changing.
After a change one side clearly grows, until a new equilibrium is set up.

en.q: Why must you wait for the temperature to return to room temperature before comparing colors?
en.concl: Before the temperature recovers, the color includes the effect of temperature and the reading is too high; to study the effect of concentration you must keep temperature the same (textbook "Questions and Discussion" item 1: control variables, compare).
points: The temperature hasn't recovered, so the color includes a temperature effect.
Turned on, the reading is 26.978, 2.09 times the true 12.878.
Textbook requirement: temperature must be the same when studying the effect of concentration.

en.q: Assessment: can you bring the red to c ≥ 1.00 mmol/L and hold it?
en.concl: Choose the right reagent, add the textbook's amount (FeCl₃ 5 drops → 1.095 mmol/L), and judge by c rather than "how dark the color looks".
points: Choose the right bottle: FeCl₃ 5 drops → 1.095; KSCN 5 drops gives only 0.720.
Passing is judged by c, not "how dark it looks".
A few more drops also pass (10 drops → 1.440).
